newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Survey shows fall in Brazil roasted coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows fall in Brazil roasted coffee sales.

text.p: A survey by Brazil's Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union of 12 companies showed a drop in roasted coffee sales of 0.6 percent in March compared with February and of three percent on March 1996, the union said.
However, in the 12 months to March 1997, sales by the 12 firms were still 17.8 percent higher than in the corresponding period in 1995/96, reaching 2.18 million bags.
During the first quarter of this year, sales totaled 505,000 bags, a rise of 7.5 percent on January to March 1996, the union said in a statement.
Consumers prices have now stopped rising and are steady at around six to 6.50 reais a kilo ($5.66-6.13) of roasted and ground coffee.
"These results, for the president of the union, show that the rise in prices up to now has been absorbed by the consumer," the statement said.

"We feel however that current prices represent the limit of consumers' preference for coffee. Higher prices than we are seeing at the present time could lead to a move toward other alternatives," said union president Nathan Herszkowicz. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
